title: 2. Store Securely
text:
Store credentials securely
The REDCap URI and API token should be stored outside the R or SAS program and outside the project directory.

Windows User variablesSecure file / .Renviron


Create the REDCap URI and project-specific token under Windows User variables.

redcap_uri → REDCap API web address
token_xxx → project-specific REDCap token








Note



After adding or changing the variables, completely close and reopen R, Positron, RStudio, or SAS before testing them.



Check that the token is available
R
nchar(Sys.getenv("token_xxx"))
SAS
%put Token length=%length(%sysget(token_xxx));



Store credentials in a protected .txt file or .Renviron in a secure location outside the project directory and do not track the file with Git.

R example, .Renviron
(This is my typical workflow when working with R; I stored my .Renviron file in Documents so it’s always backed up on OneDrive. I sometimes also put root paths in there when automating so you only have to update one place ever, and nothing is hard coded in files along the way [you can also have R/SAS detect your root. When it comes to automations, relative roots via the here package can run into issues.])
Open the user-level .Renviron file:
usethis::edit_r_environ()
Add the REDCap URI and project-specific token:
redcap_uri="https://redcap.ucdenver.edu/api/"
token_xxx="YOUR_PROJECT_TOKEN"






Important



Restart R after adding or changing values in .Renviron.


The program can then retrieve the stored values when it runs:
redcap_uri <- Sys.getenv("redcap_uri")
token <- Sys.getenv("token_xxx")


R packages for API calls

REDCapR: R utilities for interacting with REDCap
qualtRics: Introduction to qualtRics

title: Key Terms
text:
How a REDCap API workflow starts



REDCap API workflow showing one-time API access and token storage followed by repeated R or SAS requests and responses




Key terms


API
Application Programming Interface. A structured way for one system to request data from another system.


API token
A unique secret used to authorize access to a particular REDCap project.


Endpoint / URI
The web address that receives the API request.


Request
The call sent to REDCap, including the token and requested export settings.


Response
The data returned by REDCap after the request is processed.


Environment variable
A value stored outside the program and retrieved when the program runs.

title: 1. Get Token
text:
In the appropriate REDCap project, select API from the Applications section of the left sidebar.



Select Obtain API token for the project.
If you don’t see API on the left, you just need to obtain the appropriate permission from the owner or add the permission yourself if you can.



REDCap API token request screen


Once requested, it may take a few hours to appear. Once it does, your token will look like this:



API token








ImportantToken handling




Do not share the token with other people.
Do not include the token in screenshots.
Do not place the token in R or SAS code.
Do not commit the token to Git.
When the project is complete, the token should be deleted; it can generated again later if needed.
If you ever suspect your token has been exposed, delete it and generate a new one. All you have to do is update the token value whereever you stored it, and your code will continue to function.

title: 3. Call REDCap
text:
Retrieve a REDCap report
The complete runnable programs are available on the Code & Downloads page.

RSAS



Retrieve credentials
Read the REDCap URI and project token from the stored environment variables:
redcap_uri <- Sys.getenv("redcap_uri")
token <- Sys.getenv("token_toy")


Request the report
Use REDCapR::redcap_report() to retrieve the REDCap report.
raw0 <- REDCapR::redcap_report(
  redcap_uri = redcap_uri,
  token = token,
  report_id = REPORT_ID
)$data


Save the raw extract
Write the retrieved data to a dated CSV file in DataRaw.
The source extract should be preserved unchanged.




Retrieve credentials
Read the REDCap URI and project token using %sysget():
url="%sysget(redcap_uri)"
"token=%sysget(token_toy)"


Submit the API request
Use PROC HTTP to send the request to REDCap.


Save the raw extract
Import the response and save the resulting dataset in DataRaw.
The source extract should be preserved unchanged.










TipExpected result



The toy REDCap report produces 100 records and 14 variables. The source extract is saved in DataRaw.








ImportantPreserve the raw data



Do not clean, recode, deduplicate, or otherwise change the source extract while writing it to DataRaw.

title: Automation
text:
Automation with Windows Task Scheduler
After testing the API extraction manually, the same program can be scheduled to run automatically.

RSAS



R automation with taskscheduleR
The taskscheduleR package can create the initial Windows scheduled task directly from R.


1. Create the scheduled task
Use taskscheduleR::taskscheduler_create() to schedule the R script.
taskscheduleR::taskscheduler_create(
    taskname = "REDCap_API_test"
    , rscript = "Code/01_get_redcap_R.R"
    , schedule = "DAILY"
    , starttime = "09:10"
    , startdate = format(Sys.Date()+1, "%d/%m/%Y")
    )


2. Review Windows Task Scheduler
Open the created task in Windows Task Scheduler and adjust its properties as needed.
I usually do at least the following:
1. In Windows Task Scheduler, in the top left make sure you’re in the folder Task Scheduler Library
2. Find your task based on what you named it. In this instance, it’d be REDCAP_API_test. Double click on the name (or use Properties on the right)
3. I update the following:
a. General: Run whether user is logged on or not
b. Conditions > Power: Uncheck “Start the task only if the computer is on AC power”
c. (OPTIONAL) You can also go into Actions and select where the program starts from, might be helpful in instances with relative paths in the code (and the R package taskscheduleR doesn’t play nicely with the here::here() package either).
It might seem like a pain to still have to go into Task Scheduler after using taskscheduleR, so why not just do it in Windows from the start? Just personal preference, nothing more. I like to have as much traceable code as possible, but there are many other ways to do it!


3. Run the extraction
The scheduled R program retrieves the stored credentials and writes the REDCap extract to DataRaw.




SAS automation
A SAS program can be run in batch mode and launched by Windows Task Scheduler.


1. Create a batch command
Use the SAS executable to run the .sas program in batch mode.
"C:\Program Files\SASHome\SASFoundation\9.4\sas.exe" ^
  -sysin "C:\path\to\Code\01_get_redcap_sas.sas" ^
  -log "C:\path\to\Logs\redcap_api.log"
The SAS executable location varies by installation. Replace the example paths with the paths on the computer running the scheduled task.


2. Create the scheduled task
Configure Windows Task Scheduler to run the batch command on the desired schedule. See the R section above for how I typically update the task’s properties.


3. Run the extraction
The scheduled SAS program retrieves the stored credentials and writes the REDCap extract to DataRaw.










NoteProject-relative paths



Use project-relative paths so scheduled programs can reliably locate DataRaw and other project folders.








ImportantWindows password changes



A Windows password change may interrupt scheduled processing. Open the task properties and re-enter the updated password when prompted.

title: Reuse
text:
Reusable approaches
After the basic extraction works, the same pattern can be reused across reports and projects.

RSAS



Function
Store the repeated API logic in a function rather than duplicating the extraction code for each report.

Pass the report ID as an argument.
Pass the desired output filename or dataset name.
Retrieve the stored REDCap URI and token when the function runs.
Use project-relative output paths.
Preserve the unchanged source extract in DataRaw.





Macro and SASAUTOS
Store the repeated extraction logic in a SAS macro.

Store the extraction macro in Code/macros.
Add the macro folder to SASAUTOS.
Pass the report ID and output name to the macro.
Reuse the same secure connection pattern.
Preserve the unchanged source extract in DataRaw.











Note



Reusable functions and macros reduce duplicated setup and make the same extraction pattern available across multiple reports.
